evidence.testName: the board model built from the parsed registry and the four assets yields exactly 48 cells

results.note: Cell count asserted as board.families.length * board.assets.length, not the literal 48; families.length(12) and assets.length(4) are themselves derived from the real registry.yaml and BOARD_ASSETS.

evidence.testName: every one of the 48 cells carries a state and none is undefined or empty

results.note: Loops over all cells from buildBoard (pure model, no rendering) asserting state is defined, not empty, and status truthy.

evidence.testName: a family with no registry entry for an asset yields NOT_FETCHED and never NOT_DEFINABLE

results.note: Directly exercises the daily_close gap for ETH/SOL/BNB (the real US-412 shape) and asserts NOT_FETCHED, explicitly asserting NOT_DEFINABLE never appears.

evidence.testName: a registry key that does not begin with its own lowercased asset throws

results.note: familyOf (board.ts:29-37) throws on a prefix mismatch with no try/catch anywhere in buildBoard to silently swallow it; the malformed-entry test asserts the throw.

evidence.testName: a cell whose registry entry exists but whose board row is missing is also NOT_FETCHED

results.note: Registered-but-unfetched (this test) and unregistered (C3's test) both resolve to the identical UNAVAILABLE/NOT_FETCHED state via board.ts:71-74, so neither absence variety is distinguished as settled.

evidence.testName: the model maps OK STALE UNAVAILABLE and ERROR rows onto their cells without altering the value

results.note: Asserts cell.state deep-equals the input Datapoint rows unchanged (values, reasons, detail preserved) — the model in board.ts only keys/looks up and defaults, it never derives or transforms a value.

note: All seven criteria are backed by concrete, assertion-heavy tests in web/src/board.test.ts that exercise the real ingest/registry.yaml (45 entries, 12 families, 4 assets, 48 cells) against the pure buildBoard model in web/src/board.ts. No fallback/try-catch masks the malformed-key throw, and the pass-through test proves the model doesn't compute derived values. No signs of padding or assertion-free tests.
